title: Harvest date
what: The day each Block is picked. Each day of hang time trades acidity for sugar, riper fruit and riper tannin, while rot and rain risk grow.

steps: the berry respires malic acid and its skin softens as sugar rises
so acidity falls while botrytis risk climbs

choose: Pick for style, not the calendar. Kabinett needs 73 °Oe; Auslese needs 88 °Oe, so a longer hang. In warm sites sugar outruns the seeds: waiting means more alcohol, less acid. In cool sites waiting risks rot and rain, and early-picked Cabernet keeps green-pepper pyrazines.
exam: Questions ask how harvest timing shapes style, often cool against warm regions. Link date → sugar, acid, tannin or pyrazines → alcohol, acidity, aroma.

check.question: A cool Mosel autumn: your Riesling Block is at 76 °Oe with TA 9.5 g/L, and rain is forecast all week. You want a Kabinett. What is the better call?
options: Pick now: Kabinett weight is reached and rot risk only grows
Wait a week for Spätlese weight; the rain will concentrate the sugar
Wait: botrytis on ripe Riesling turns noble and adds sugar
Wait: cool weather keeps the acid, so a week costs nothing
check.answer: Pick now: Kabinett weight is reached and rot risk only grows
check.why: 76 °Oe already passes the 73 °Oe Kabinett minimum. Ripe, softening berries in wet weather are at their most susceptible to grey rot, not noble rot, and acidity only falls with hang time. Rain swells the berries and dilutes the juice; it never concentrates it.
